candidates.statement: Open-set RF fingerprinting lacks validation under dynamic real-world channel/environment variation such as human motion, multipath, device orientation, and distance changes.
candidates.rationale: The original RF augmentation paper uses a bounded testbed and motivates a question about generalization beyond that environment.

candidates.statement: Can blind generative outlier augmentation for open-set RF fingerprinting avoid both manually tuned generation hyperparameters and large computational cost while retaining comparable open-set accuracy?
candidates.rationale: The exact-source evidence shows a tradeoff between delta tuning and roughly 30x outlier-generation cost.

counterevidence.title: Dynamic and Open-Set RF Fingerprinting and Localization in Crowded Indoor Environments through Contrastive Channel State Information Learning
counterevidence.observed_coverage: Abstract explicitly evaluates open-set RF authentication under human motion, multipath, device orientation, and distance variation.

challenges.reasoning: The broad gap is directly covered by later prior work and must be rejected rather than rescued through semantic narrowing.

counterevidence.title: Out-of-Distribution (OOD) Detectors for Open-Set RF Fingerprinting
counterevidence.observed_coverage: Abstract reports open-set RFF OOD detectors that can be tuned without supplied OOD tuning data, attacking the same operational constraint through a non-generative method.

challenges.reasoning: The broader no-known-outlier problem is partially addressed by later OOD work, so the surviving hypothesis must be narrowed to efficient blind generative augmentation specifically.
